# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

# [ms] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:350b88ed1730⟧
Mode: Code Development (code)

Legend: 🎯session ●bugfix ◆feature ↻refactor ✓change ○discovery ⚖decision ⚠security_alert ⚷security_note ⊘sensitive
Format: ID TIME TYPE TITLE
Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 2 obs (955t read) | 19,574t work | 95% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
4 10:34a ○ ms package unit parsing structure mapped in src/index.ts
5 10:35a ◆ ms() now parses microsecond units (us, µs, μs, microsecond, microseconds)
S1 Add microsecond support to ms() with units us, µs, microsecond, and microseconds, so ms("500us") returns 0.5; update unit types, README unit list, and add tests. (Nov 3, 10:35 AM)
**Investigated**: Mapped the unit-handling structure of src/index.ts (unit constants, string-literal unit types, the parse regex, and the exhaustive switch) and the README unit documentation. Reviewed the existing parse tests in src/parse.test.ts.

**Learned**: Units are defined as string-literal union types that feed both the Unit union and StringValue. The parse() regex must include each new alias or it won't match. The switch uses a `satisfies never` default, so a new unit type without a matching case fails type-checking. The milliseconds branch returns the raw value, so microseconds need division by 1000. The README lists units in a type block that must stay in sync with the code.

**Completed**: Added a Microseconds type to src/index.ts and included it in the Unit union. Extended the parse regex and switch so microsecond aliases return n / 1000. Added Microseconds to the README type block. Added a "should convert microseconds to ms" test in src/parse.test.ts covering us, µs, μs, microsecond(s), a space before the unit, upper and mixed case, a fractional value, and a negative value. The type-check passes, and the full Jest suite passes with 168 of 168 tests and 100% coverage. The diff touches 3 files with 22 insertions and 3 deletions.

**Next Steps**: The observed session has reported the work as complete and is awaiting further requests. Any follow-up would be a new request, not ongoing edits.

**Notes**: The observed session also accepted the μs spelling (Greek mu, U+03BC) alongside the µs micro sign (U+00B5), which was not in the original request. Formatting was intentionally left unchanged, so ms(0.5) still returns "0.5ms". The README prose section on fractional values was not reported as updated; only the type block was.


Access 20k tokens of past work via get_observations([IDs]) or mem-search skill.
